data.body:
STATUS CHECK: 5 of 6 ACs are done, and the remaining one is BLOCKED ON EPIC 6202 rather than waiting for anyone to pick it up.

AC4 reads: 'root usage has a bounded CEILING, not merely a faster reclaim -- a mechanism that cannot
exceed a configured high-water mark regardless of build burst rate.' That is precisely what epic 6202
(endowed-upset-scaup) is building, and it is not something this ticket can satisfy independently.

Epic progress toward that ceiling as of now:
 - S0 (ADR 0112) -- MERGED and closed. Establishes that a cap below peak concurrent hold cannot be
   honoured by reclamation at all, because the janitor reclaims by high-water mark over POSIX
   delete-on-last-close, so bytes held by an in-flight gate are LIVE rather than garbage.
 - S6 (bounded gate admission) -- MERGED and closed. This is the PRECONDITION for every cap: without
   it, a ceiling below peak concurrent hold is unenforceable by construction.
 - S1 (dedicated gate-scratch EBS volume) -- MERGED and closed. Moves the largest gate accumulator off
   root entirely.
 - S2 (Docker overlay2 + BuildKit cap, per-generator alarms) -- dispatched, in plan review.
 - S3 (journald), S4 (/var/tmp), S5 (container layers) -- unblocked and queued. All four share
   compose-up.sh, observability.sh, monitoring_autodeploy.tf and review-bot-ops.md, so they are being
   run ONE AT A TIME rather than in parallel.

AC4 becomes verifiable once S2-S5 land, since only then does every accumulator have a bound and the
'plateaus below the bound' simulation the AC asks for becomes meaningful. Verifying it now would test
a partial ceiling and produce a number that means nothing.

Recording this so the ticket does not read as stalled work. It is not waiting on attention; it is
waiting on four sibling stories, three of which have already landed this session.
